q: how many ml of Tylenol for a 22 pound baby
text:
22 lb = 10 kg.

Paracetamol (acetaminophen) for 10 kg:
• Dose: 150 mg every 4–6 h (max 4 doses/day).
  – Tylenol Children's / Infants', syrup 160 mg/5 ml: 4.6 ml
  – syrup 120 mg/5 ml: 6.2 ml
  – syrup 125 mg/5 ml: 6 ml
  – syrup 150 mg/5 ml (3 %): 5 ml
  – syrup 200 mg/5 ml (4 %): 3.7 ml
  – syrup 250 mg/5 ml: 3 ml
  – drops 100 mg/5 ml: 7.5 ml
  – drops 100 mg/ml: 1.5 ml
  – drops 200 mg/ml: 0.7 ml
The guide allows 100–150 mg; this is the usual dose for fever.

q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old, according to MedlinePlus [6]. It helps reduce fever, and is usually given every 6 to 8 hours [6]. Do not give it to a child who is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it, according to the NHS [3]. Check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine suits your child, or ask a pharmacist if you are unsure [4].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text: Give small sips of an oral rehydration solution, which you can buy without a prescription, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The SEUP recommends waiting 20 minutes after a vomit, then giving 2–5 ml of oral rehydration solution every 5 minutes for an hour, and increasing the frequency if he keeps it down [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Keep offering his normal food in smaller, more frequent amounts, and avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices [2]. See a doctor if he vomits a lot, cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits green, bloody or coffee-ground material [2].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [1]. Signs to watch for are a child who is drowsy or listless, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or passes little urine [7]. If you notice any of these, or if your child vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, they should be seen [7].

To help prevent it, offer oral rehydration solution: after a vomit, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, and increase slowly if it is well tolerated [4]. Avoid homemade solutions and fizzy drinks [4].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is often a sign of the bronchi narrowing, and in preschool children the most frequent trigger is a viral cold [1]. The SEUP describes these episodes as cough, breathlessness and a whistling sound when breathing out, sometimes starting after a cold or exercise [5]. If your child has been diagnosed with asthma, inhaled medicines such as salbutamol relieve this narrowing, and inhalers must always be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth [1][7].

See a doctor urgently if your child is very restless or drowsy, turns blue or pale, breathes faster and faster, or needs inhalations every two hours or less [7].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough lasting about a week after a cold is common, and some symptoms of a cold can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough is barking and sounds like a seal, or comes with a hoarse voice or noisy breathing, that points to croup, according to the NHS [2]. A cough that comes in bouts and is worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" or vomiting after coughing, suggests whooping cough, according to the NHS [4].

See a doctor if your child is struggling to breathe, has blue, grey or pale skin, lips or tongue, is sleepier than normal or difficult to wake, or is unusually quiet and still [7].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text: A cough without fever, with normal eating, is not one of the warning signs the NHS lists for a child who needs urgent help [1]. A high temperature in children is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds [1]. Keep offering fluids and let them rest; a poor appetite for a few days is not harmful [3]. See your doctor if your child does not want to eat, is not their usual self and you are worried, or has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly can have several causes, and the pattern matters more than the colour. Raised, itchy patches or spots could be hives, which can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [5]. Chickenpox spots can be anywhere on the body, including inside the mouth, and may be red, pink or darker than the surrounding skin [4]. Measles also causes a red, blotchy rash, often with fever, cough, runny nose and conjunctivitis, according to MedlinePlus [2].

See a doctor if your daughter has swelling around her mouth or is struggling to breathe [5].

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text: Itchy red bumps on the legs in a small child can be scabies, which causes severe itching that is often worse at night, along with bumps and itchy lines on the fingers, wrists, arms, legs and belt area, according to the WHO [5]. In infants and small children the rash can be larger, including on the palms, soles, ankles and scalp [5]. Scratching can let bacteria into the skin and cause impetigo, so it is worth having your child seen. Eczema is another common cause of dry, itchy skin in children, and scratching makes it redder and itchier, according to MedlinePlus [1]. See your doctor so the rash can be looked at and treated properly.

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text: Spots that don't bother her and keep appearing each morning are common in nappy rash, according to the NHS: red or raw patches on the bottom or nappy area, sometimes with spots, pimples or blisters, and the skin may look scaly and dry [1][2]. It can usually be treated at home [2]. If the spots are instead dry and itchy, eczema is another common cause in babies and young children, and it is not contagious [6]. See your doctor if the rash spreads, blisters, or she becomes uncomfortable or distressed [1].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. After a blow to the head, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

Watch him over the next 24 hours for warning signs, and get urgent medical help if any appear [2][5]:

- He was knocked out, cannot stay awake, or has a seizure [2]
- Repeated vomiting, worsening headache, confusion, or trouble speaking or walking [4]
- Clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears, or bruising behind the ears [2][4]

He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. Rest from sport and screens for 24 to 48 hours, then return gradually to normal activity [4]. If you are worried about any symptom, have him seen [5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text: At around 6 months, milk still gives your baby most of their energy and nutrients while they get used to eating, according to the NHS [2]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and offer foods one at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting [1][3]. Keep breastfeeding or formula feeding alongside the food [2][3]. There are foods to avoid for now: no honey and no cow's milk before 12 months, and no unpasteurised drinks or foods [1]. Also avoid choking hazards like sweets, popcorn, whole nuts and whole grapes until age 3 [1]. Ask your baby's pediatrician if you have questions, especially about peanut products or if your baby was born prematurely [1][2].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and the AEP recommends keeping it on demand, without reducing the number of feeds [2]. Water is not needed in large amounts at this age: the AEP notes that babies need very little salt because their kidneys are still immature, and the same caution applies to how much they drink beyond milk [2]. Offer water in a cup with meals, but let your baby decide how much — the AEP says the caregiver offers healthy food and drink and the baby decides the amount [6]. If your baby is unwell, the WHO advises increasing fluids, including more frequent breastfeeding [1]. Ask your doctor if you are worried about how much your baby is drinking.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: A baby refusing vegetables while eating fruit all day is common, and the AEP advises offering the whole variety of fruits and vegetables progressively, at any daily meal, varying how they are presented — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [2]. There are no better fruits than others to start with; it depends on the family's tastes [2]. Taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is shaped early, and early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [2]. Fruit juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods, so whole fruit is recommended [2]. Keep offering vegetables without forcing, alongside the fruit.

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula should be a complement to food, not the main source of nutrition: complementary feeding means offering solid or liquid foods other than breast milk or infant formula as a complement, not as a replacement for it, according to the AEP [2]. From 6 months onwards, nutritionally adequate and safe complementary foods should be introduced while milk feeding continues [1]. The WHO recommends breastfeeding continue up to 2 years or beyond alongside those foods [1], and the first two years are especially important because optimal nutrition during this period reduces illness and supports growth and development [3]. If you are concerned about how much she is eating or her growth, speak to your doctor.

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: It is not essential for a baby to pass a stool every day: the rhythm and consistency of stools varies from one person to another, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more than the number is the consistency — constipation is when stools become excessively hard, with discomfort or incomplete passing, and it may come with fewer stools than usual [6]. In a baby under 6 months, keep the usual feeding with breast milk or formula [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of abdominal pain, or repeated vomiting with no tolerance of solids or liquids [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text: Waking every two hours at night is common at this age: night wakings are physiological, and around 30% of children still wake at night by their first birthday, according to the PUC Chile manual [1]. Each sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes, so brief wakings between cycles are expected [1]. If your baby always falls asleep in your arms, they will look for that same condition to fall back asleep, so the manual suggests letting them settle themselves rather than intervening, to avoid creating a sleep habit [1]. Insomnia in infants is most often due to habits rather than illness [4]. If your baby seems unwell, is feeding poorly, or the waking comes with fever or breathing problems, see your doctor.

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on at night or early in the morning is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Other signs include chest tightness, shortness of breath or rapid breathing, wheezing (a whistling sound when breathing out), feeling tired, and trouble eating [4]. These symptoms can be mild or severe, and may happen often or only once in a while [4].

See a doctor if the coughing is severe, if he has serious breathing problems, or if he turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [4].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text: Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual is one of the signs that needs medical review: the SEUP says to seek urgent care if inhalations are needed very frequently, every two hours or less [6]. Salbutamol opens the airways and relieves symptoms, and most mild attacks can be managed at home with it [2][3]. It should always be given through a spacer, never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [6]. Watch for breathing that gets faster, ribs or chest pulling in, or a bluish colour around the lips — these mean it is getting worse [5][6]. If there is no clear improvement, the child needs to be seen at a health centre [6].

q: my daughter is breathing faster after running but gets better when she rests
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Fast breathing during running that settles with rest is expected — the SEUP lists fast breathing as a sign to watch for when it appears at rest or with tiredness in everyday activity, not as the normal quick breathing of exercise [2]. What matters is how she looks once she has stopped and calmed down.

Watch for breathing that stays fast at rest, ribs pulling in or the chest dipping, or tiredness out of proportion to the effort [2][3]. If any of those appear, she needs to be seen.

If she is otherwise well, with no fever, she can keep up her normal activity and school routine [2].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy, high-pitched breathing and a barking cough, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold and the symptoms usually get worse at night, lasting three to five days [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3].

See a doctor promptly if you are worried about her breathing, or if she has trouble breathing, is drowsy, or is very irritable [3][4].

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text: Chest pain when breathing deeply is one of the warning signs to watch for at home, according to the SEUP: it can mean the child is getting worse, along with breathing difficulty such as ribs showing, the chest sinking in, fast breathing or tiring when walking or running [1]. The SEUP also lists chest or side pain when breathing as a reason to go to the emergency department, to rule out complications [5]. Asthma can cause chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply, and symptoms are often worse at night or with exercise [2]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor straight away [4].

q: my daughter is crying nonstop after a fall and wont calm down
text:
After a blow to the head, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1]. Most head injuries are mild and not dangerous, but you should watch your daughter for the first 24 hours [2].

Seek help immediately if there is worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion or agitation, drowsiness, weakness, or trouble speaking or walking, according to MedlinePlus [4].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. They usually last 2 to 3 minutes and affect children between 6 months and 6 years old [2]. Your child will need to be checked in hospital after a first febrile seizure, and may need to stay in for a short time [6].

While a seizure is happening: do not move your child or hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to cool them by undressing them or sponging with cold water [5].

Get medical help if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if your child has trouble breathing, if the stiffness and twitching are on only one side, if they are more sleepy than usual for over an hour afterwards, or if they have more than one seizure within 24 hours [2].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A febrile seizure is not usually serious and is unlikely to have harmed your child or caused long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. Children who have had one have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, but this is rare [3]. It does not mean your child will keep having seizures, and you cannot prevent them [3].

See a doctor if your child has another seizure, especially if it lasts more than 5 minutes, affects only one side of the body, or leaves them more sleepy than usual for over an hour afterwards [5].

q: my child has a sore throat and white stuff on the tonsils
text:
A sore throat with white patches on the tonsils can be tonsillitis, an infection of the tonsils that is a common childhood illness, according to the NHS [1]. Along with the sore throat and white patches, children may have a high temperature, problems swallowing, a cough, a headache, earache or feel tired [1]. Sore throats are usually caused by viruses and normally get better by themselves within a week [4][6]. To help soothe it, offer plenty of water and cool or soft foods, and let them rest [6].

See a doctor if the symptoms do not go away within 1 week, or if your child keeps getting throat infections [2].

q: when should I take my kid to the doctor for a sore throat
text:
A sore throat is very common and usually nothing to worry about — it normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [5]. In children it can also come with a high temperature and seem less active than usual [4].

See a doctor if your child is under 5 and needs help for a sore throat, or if it does not improve after a week [2]. Get urgent help if there is difficulty breathing or swallowing, drooling, a high-pitched sound when breathing, or symptoms that are severe and getting worse quickly [2].

Some children feel nauseous, sweaty, or have blurred vision just before it happens, which can help them recognise it and sit or lie down in time [1].

See a doctor if the fainting happened during exercise or effort, or while sitting; if it lasted more than 3 to 5 minutes; or if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the limbs, or passing urine [6].

It is one of the most common infections in young children [5].

See a doctor if your child becomes very drowsy, sleepy or very irritable, or has trouble breathing [4].

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly

text: A blocked nose and trouble feeding are common with a cold: sneezing, a blocked nose, runny nose, sore throat and cough usually start a few days after infection and some symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [3]. To help, use saline nose drops from a pharmacy if the nose is blocked, and offer smaller feeds more often [4]. Keeping the nose clear with nasal washes and feeding little and often also help keep feeding and hydration good, according to the SEUP [2]. If there is a high temperature and your baby is uncomfortable, children's paracetamol or ibuprofen can be given — check the leaflet to make sure it is suitable [4].

q: my 2 year old has a temperature of 39.2 and cold hands
text:
A temperature of 39.2°C with cold hands is common when a fever is rising, and the NHS says a child over 3 months with a temperature of 39°C or higher should be seen urgently [6]. Keep offering plenty of fluids and check their temperature, and if they are uncomfortable with a fever above 38°C you can give the antipyretic your paediatrician usually recommends [2].

Watch for these signs, which mean they need to be seen:
- Difficulty breathing, breathing fast, or the ribs pulling in [4][6]
- Being very drowsy, floppy, or very irritable [4][6]
- A dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or other signs of dehydration [6]

q: can I give Nurofen as well
text: No, not at the same time. Do not give ibuprofen and paracetamol together, according to the NHS [6]. You can alternate between them, but only if a health professional such as a doctor or nurse tells you to [6]. If they do, write down when you gave each medicine so the doses are spaced evenly [6]. q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
Stomach ache with refusing food is common in children, and the SEUP says abdominal pain is usually transient [7]. It can come with fever, vomiting, diarrhoea or cough, and sometimes it is caused by illnesses outside the belly, like tonsillitis, a cold, pneumonia or an ear infection [1]. Gastroenteritis — an infection of the digestive tract — often causes abdominal pain, vomiting and fever alongside loose stools [3], and MedlinePlus lists belly pain or cramps among its symptoms [5].

See a doctor if your child is generally unwell, pale or very low on energy, or is refusing food markedly [7].

q: my 8 month old hasnt had a wet nappy since this morning
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more is a sign of dehydration in babies, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Other signs to watch for are a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, unusual sleepiness or irritability, and sunken eyes [6]. Dehydration happens when a child loses more fluid than they take in, often from diarrhoea, vomiting or fever [3].

Keep offering fluids: for mild cases, frequent small amounts of water, and oral rehydration solutions for children are available without a prescription [4]. If your baby is breastfed, keep feeding normally and offer the breast more often if they want it [1]. Avoid sugary drinks and juices [1].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text: A fever is a temperature above 38°C and is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. For a baby this age, the NHS advises getting medical advice: a temperature of 38°C or higher in a baby under 3 months, or 39°C or higher in a baby of 3 to 6 months, needs urgent assessment [7]. While you wait, keep breastfeeding or offering fluids as normal, do not undress or sponge your baby to cool them, and do not give them too many clothes or bedclothes [2][7]. Do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months or under 5 kg, and do not give paracetamol to a baby under 2 months [7]. Get medical advice if your baby is not feeding, is not their usual self, has a rash, or is dehydrated [7].

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, fever can follow vaccination and is usually not a sign that anything is wrong. The recommended vaccines are given at well-child visits, following the vaccination schedule, according to MedlinePlus [3]. In India, the ages and doses follow India's national immunisation schedule, which may differ from the schedules published in other countries [3].

Give plenty of fluids and keep your child comfortable. The dose of any fever medicine depends on your child's age and weight, so ask your doctor or follow the leaflet for the correct amount.

See a doctor if the fever is high, lasts more than a few days, or your child is drowsy, breathing fast, or not drinking.

text:
Vomiting after a head injury is one of the signs that needs to be checked in the emergency department, according to the SEUP [1]. The medical team will do the examinations they consider necessary and decide whether any extra tests are needed, although in most cases these are not necessary [1].

While you are on the way, keep your son with you and do not give him anything to eat or drink unless a doctor tells you to [1]. If he becomes drowsy, floppy, or is hard to wake, tell the staff as soon as you arrive [2].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Mosquito bites usually itch, and most insect bites are not usually serious and get better in a few days, according to MedlinePlus [1][2]. To stop the itch getting worse, do not let her scratch the bites, as scratching can make them infected [7]. A pharmacist can suggest treatments such as antihistamines and steroid creams for the itch [7].

See a doctor if the skin around a bite feels hot or looks red, is painful or swollen, or has pus or fluid coming out, or if she has a high temperature with swollen glands [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text: A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and the organisations describe them rather than a nebulizer. A cough that is worse at night can be part of whooping cough, which starts like a cold and then brings coughing bouts that are worse at night, according to the NHS [2]. Asthma also causes coughing that is worse at night or early in the morning, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Croup causes a barking, seal-like cough and is often worse at night, according to the NHS [3]. None of these say to use a nebulizer at home; that is a treatment your doctor decides on. See your doctor if the cough is getting worse or is not getting better [7].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
A child who keeps being sick and cannot keep fluid down needs to be seen today [2][3]. While you wait, offer oral rehydration solution in small, frequent sips rather than a full glass at once, and keep breastfeeding or formula feeding as usual if your son is on milk [7]. Do not water down formula, and avoid fruit juice, fizzy drinks and sports drinks, which can make vomiting worse [5][7].

See a doctor urgently if the vomit is green, contains blood or looks like coffee grounds, or if your son is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine [4][5].

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
banner: 💛 यह ज़रूरी है और आप अकेले नहीं हैं। Tele-MANAS 14416 पर कॉल करें (या 112 पर अगर खतरा अभी है)। अगर बच्चे ने खुद को नुकसान पहुँचाया है, तो अभी इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: खानपान के विकार के संकेत
text:
दस्त में बच्चे को खाना खिलाना बंद नहीं करना चाहिए — डब्ल्यूएचओ के अनुसार पोषक तत्वों से भरपूर खाना, जिसमें मां का दूध भी शामिल है, दस्त के दौरान भी जारी रखना चाहिए [2]। इलाज में ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) का घोल और ज़िंक की खुराक दोनों शामिल हैं; ज़िंक दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% तक कम करता है [2]। SEUP के मुताबिक उपवास ज़रूरी नहीं है — बच्चा लगभग सामान्य खाना खाता रहे, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, उसकी भूख का सम्मान करते हुए [6]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें; दही-दूध जैसे डेयरी उत्पाद ज़रूरी नहीं कि हटाएं, और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [6]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]। खून वाले दस्त, लंबे समय तक चलने वाले दस्त या निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों में भी स्वास्थ्यकर्मी से सलाह लें [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह के छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे हुए लाल दाने निकलते हैं, जो फफोले बन सकते हैं — यह NHS के अनुसार है [3]। यह आमतौर पर 7 से 10 दिन में खुद ठीक हो जाता है और इसका कोई दवा से इलाज नहीं है [1]। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद चेहरे पर बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर नीचे की ओर फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है — यह CDC के अनुसार है [4]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और उससे पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार और बेचैनी हो सकती है [5]।

दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें। अगर दाने के साथ मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या बच्चे को साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नहीं, यह हल्के में लेने वाली बात नहीं है — कम पेशाब और कम दूध पीना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [1]।

तब तक, SEUP के अनुसार, बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी ज़्यादा बार कराते रहें [1]। मुँह से दिया जाने वाला ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन घोल (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दें, ताकि उल्टी का जोखिम कम हो [1]। खेल-कूद वाले पेय (स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक) और जूस न दें, क्योंकि उनमें शक्कर बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट का संतुलन बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होता है [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाएँ [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है। SEUP के अनुसार अगर बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है, या गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई है, तो भी तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना चाहिए [1]। डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और देखेंगे कि आगे कोई टेस्ट चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

रास्ते में बच्चे को होश में रखने की कोशिश करें और उल्टी होने पर उसे करवट पर लिटाएँ ताकि कुछ भी साँस की नली में न जाए। अगर बच्चा सुस्त लगे, बेहोश हो जाए, बार-बार उल्टी करे, या उसका व्यवहार चिंता की बात लगे, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन सेवा से संपर्क करें [1]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ के कारण बच्चा पॉटी करते समय रो सकता है — रोने के आम कारणों में कब्ज़ भी शामिल है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]। अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे चुप नहीं करा पा रहे, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है [4]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा रोते-रोते पीला पड़ जाए, पसीना आए, सुस्त लगे या दूध पीना छोड़ दे, या उसे बुखार हो, उल्टी हो या पॉटी में खून आए [6]।

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ke lakshan ho sakte hain — chhote, ubhre hue dane aur khujli wali feeling iske aam lakshan hain, NHS ke mutabik [6]. Heat rash aam taur par kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6]. Ise thanda rakhna sabse zaroori hai: dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halki rajai use karein, aur thande paani se nahiyein [6]. Khujli kam karne ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur khujlane ke bajaye dane ko thap-thap karein [6]. Perfume wale shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Doctor se milein agar dane badh rahe hain, ya aapko yakeen nahi ki ye heat rash hai [6].

text:
Bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai to turant medical madad lena zaroori hai — SEUP ke mutabik saans lene mein takleef, pasliyan dikhna ya seene ka dhadakna, tez saans, chalne ya daudne mein thakan, ya saans lete waqt seene mein dard, in sab par turant ilaaj ki zaroorat hoti hai [7].

Kuch bachchon mein shuruaati lakshan sardi-jukam jaise hote hain — naak behna, khaansna, halka bukhaar — aur phir saans tez ho jaati hai, doodh peene ya khaane mein dikkat hoti hai, aur ghurghur ki awaaz aati hai [5]. RSV mein bhi shuruaat halki hoti hai, lekin kuch dinon mein yeh gambhir ho sakta hai, aur bachchon mein saans lene mein dikkat iska lakshan ho sakta hai [2][4].

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is a common pattern in whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, children get coughing bouts that last a few minutes and are worse at night, according to the NHS [2]. The cough may last several weeks or months [2]. In whooping cough the coughing fits get worse and happen more often, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Croup is another cause of a night-time cough — a barking cough that sounds like a seal, often worse at night, according to the NHS [5].

See a doctor if the cough is very bad and getting worse, or if your child is finding it hard to breathe properly [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text: A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by several different illnesses, and only a doctor can tell which one it is. Measles causes a red, blotchy rash that usually starts on the head and moves down the body, along with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Chickenpox also causes a widespread, itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face and chest before spreading, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Measles can lead to serious problems, and complications are more common in children under five, according to the WHO [4]. See your doctor so your child can be examined.

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling noise when breathing can be a sign of bronchiolitis, an infection of the small airways caused by a virus, most often in babies under 2 years old [4]. It usually starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and after 2 to 4 days breathing can become faster and feeding harder [6]. Wheezing noises are also more common with viral infections [7].

While you are on your way, keep feeding offered and watch their breathing, how well they take feeds, their colour and their temperature [5].

q: बुखार के लिए कितना पैरासिटामोल दे सकती हूँ?
text: बच्चे का वज़न कितना है? पैरासिटामोल की खुराक उम्र से नहीं, वज़न से तय होती है: वज़न बताइए, फिर सही मात्रा बताई जाएगी।

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में बुखार बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में खुद उतर जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]। घर पर ही देखभाल की जा सकती है: खूब तरल दें, स्तनपान जारी रखें, भूख लगे तो खाना दें, और रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या परेशान लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा इस उम्र के लिए ठीक है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, और 16 साल से कम उम्र में एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। अगर बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे, बच्चा खाना न चाहे या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का न लगे, या पेशाब कम आए — सूखी डायपर, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना — तो डॉक्टर से सलाह लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ सकते हैं, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य बताता है [3]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा है, बुखार के साथ दाने हैं, बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा से है, या बच्चा खाने को तैयार नहीं है [7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text: 3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और सीने से सीटी जैसी आवाज़ होना सांस की नली में रुकावट के कारण हो सकता है, जिसमें खांसी, सांस लेने में तकलीफ और सीने में "सिबिलेंस" (सीटी की आवाज़) शामिल हैं, और यह सालबुटामोल जैसी ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से ठीक हो सकता है [2]। प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ का सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल संक्रमण होता है [2]। अस्थमा में भी सांस की नलियां सूजकर सिकुड़ जाती हैं, जिससे सीटी की आवाज़, खांसी और सीने में जकड़न होती है [4]। अस्थमा के लक्षण हल्के या गंभीर हो सकते हैं और समय-समय पर आते-जाते रहते हैं; लक्षण दिखने पर स्वास्थ्यकर्मी से मिलना चाहिए [5]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली के साथ त्वचा में सुरंग लगाने वाले छोटे कीड़े (स्केबीज़) हो सकते हैं, जिसका इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]। स्केबीज़ एक परजीवी संक्रमण है जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देता है और तेज़ खुजली व दाने पैदा करता है, और यह त्वचा से त्वचा के संपर्क से फैलता है [2]। इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवाओं से होता है [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें यदि:
- बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो और स्केबीज़ के लक्षण हों, या घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का लगे या एक्ज़िमा जैसी कोई और त्वचा की समस्या हो [1]
- फ़ार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के हल्के दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ये सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का इलाज आसानी से हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर कर रही है [6]। nidirect के अनुसार टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं तथा गंभीर बीमारियों से बचाते हैं [4]।

भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर से लें [4]। अगर बच्चे का कोई टीका छूट गया हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाएँ [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi bachchon mein asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik asthma mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. SEUP ke mutabik bhi asthma crisis mein bachchon ko kabhi-kabhi raat ko khansi aati hai [1]. Agar saath mein saans phoolna, seene ka dhadakna, ya seeti jaisi awaaz ho, to yeh bhi isi taraf ishara karta hai [1][5].

Doctor se turant milein agar:
- Saans lene mein bahut takleef ho, seene ki pasliyan saaf dikhne lagein, ya bachcha bahut sust ya neend mein ho [7].
- Honth ya chehra neela ya bahut peela pad jaye [5][7].
- Khansi ke saath bukhar ya saans ki takleef badhti jaye [4].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text: Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko bed se girne ke baad sar par chot lagi hai, aur sar ki chot ke aam lakshan hain sar dard, bhram, ulti aur neend aana, SEUP ke mutabik [1]. Ghar par pehle 24 ghante dhyan se nigrani karein, SEUP ke mutabik [3]. Agar sar dard tez ya badhta ho, baar-baar ulti ho, ya bachcha chidchida ho ya jagaana mushkil ho, to turant doctor ke paas le jaayein, SEUP ke mutabik [2]. Doctor ke batayi hui khurak mein paracetamol ya ibuprofen diya ja sakta hai, SEUP ke mutabik [6].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas taur par raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain [1]. Chhote bachchon mein yeh rash zyada gambhir ho sakta hai, khaas taur par hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par [1].

MedlinePlus ke mutabik varicela mein bhi khujli wali rash hoti hai jo pani ki chhaale ban kar phir khuski banati hai, aur aam taur par chehre, seene aur peeth se shuru hokar poore sharir par failti hai [4]. Eccema mein twacha sookhi ho jaati hai aur khujli hoti hai, aur yeh chehra, kohni ke andar aur ghutnon ke peeche zyada hota hai [5].

Agar bachche ko tez bukhar, saans lene mein takleef, ya rash ke saath susti dikhe, to apne doctor se turant milna chahiye [3].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text: Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: bachche ko polio se bachane ke liye polio vaccine lagwana zaroori hai, aur ise samay par lagwana chahiye [3]. Spain ke vaccination calendar ke mutabik polio vaccine (VPI) 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein lagti hai, aur 6 saal ki umar par ek booster dose di jaati hai [3]. Agar bachche ko 2, 4, 6 aur 18 mahine mein chaar doses mil chuki hain, to 6 saal par polio ke bina dTpa diya jaata hai [3]. WHO ke mutabik polio vaccine doosri vaccines ke saath mila kar di jaati hai, jaise diphtheria, tetanus aur hepatitis B ke saath [6]. Agar aapke bachche ki koi dose chhoot gayi hai, to apne doctor se milein taaki pending doses poori ho sakein [3].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text: Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection of the gut, and the main treatment is to replace the water and salts lost, according to the WHO [2]. Oral rehydration salts are a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar, and zinc supplements shorten the episode and reduce stool volume [2]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [2]. Do not use homemade solutions or soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [1]. See a doctor if there is blood in the stool, persistent diarrhoea, or signs of dehydration such as crying without tears, little urine or sunken eyes [2][1].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये लक्षण आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के बाद 6-7 दिनों में हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जिनके लिए इलाज की ज़रूरत नहीं होती [5]। बुखार के लिए पैरासिटामोल दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]। अगर लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों, या इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए, तो स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी से परामर्श करें [5]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Dizziness after being in the sun can be a sign of a heat-related illness, and children are at higher risk [3]. Move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, apply cool wet cloths to the forehead, neck and armpits, and offer cool water in small sips, according to the SEUP [6]. Heat stroke is serious: it can raise body temperature above 41°C and cause dizziness, nausea and confusion, and needs medical help right away [3].

See a doctor urgently if the dizziness comes with confusion, trouble speaking or moving, loss of consciousness, or vomiting they cannot keep fluids down with [7].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text: Solid khana (weaning) baby ko taqreeban 6 mahine ki umar se shuru karna chahiye, NHS ke mutabiq [2]. Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke baby kitna khata hai — ahem yeh hai ke woh khane ki aadat pade; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh se hi milte hain [2]. 6 mahine se pehle shuru karne ki bajaye intezar karna behtar hai kyunke doodh us waqt tak zaroori energy aur nutrients deta hai, aur baby ka munh, chabana aur nigalna behtar taur par kaam karne lagta hai [4]. Doodh ke saath saath alag alag qism ke khane dene se bachay ki sehatmand khane ki aadat ban sakti hai [2]. Agar baby waqt se pehle paida hua tha, to solid khana kab shuru karna hai is par apne doctor se mashwara karein [2].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Give your child an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes lost, according to the WHO [1]. It is a mix of clean water, salt and sugar, and it is the most important step to avoid dehydration [1]. Keep offering nutritious food and breast milk during the episode [1]. q: my 3 year old has severe chest congestion and flu
text:
A chest infection is an infection of the lungs or large airways, and it often follows a cold or flu, according to the NHS [2]. The main signs are a chesty cough, sometimes with green or yellow mucus, wheezing, shortness of breath, chest pain, a high temperature, headache, aching muscles and tiredness [2]. These symptoms are unpleasant but usually get better on their own in about 7 to 10 days, and the cough and mucus can last up to 3 weeks [2]. Flu itself usually starts suddenly with fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue, and most people recover within a week, according to the WHO [3]. Rest and plenty of fluids help [3].

See a doctor if your child is breathing fast or working hard to breathe, is struggling to feed or drink, or seems very unwell [5][6].

text: Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, according to the NHS [3]. q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and says diarrhoea should be treated with ORS, a solution of clean water, sugar and salt [1][6]. q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text: El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas distintas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no está causado por un problema del corazón, según el NHS [2]. Un dolor que aparece después de hacer ejercicio o de una lesión en el pecho, que empeora al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo, puede deberse a un esguince o distensión muscular [2]. También la ansiedad o un ataque de pánico pueden provocar un dolor a menudo agudo y continuo, con latidos más rápidos, sudoración y mareos [2]. La ansiedad es una respuesta natural ante situaciones percibidas como amenazas, y sentirla de forma ocasional es normal, según la SEUP [7]. No te autodiagnostiques: si te preocupa, consulta con tu médico [2].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. El calor, el esfuerzo, el dolor o el miedo son situaciones que lo favorecen [1]. Antes de perder el conocimiento puede haber náuseas, visión borrosa, sudoración o zumbidos, y tras un rato de reposo los niños suelen recuperarse en un par de minutos [2][5].

Conviene consultar en urgencias si el desmayo ocurrió haciendo ejercicio físico o esfuerzo, si tardó más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento, o si hubo palpitaciones, dolor en el pecho, sacudidas o pérdida de orina [4].

Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación, y para que las soluciones de rehidratación oral se toleren bien hay que ofrecerlas en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, según la SEUP [6]. q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text: No hay una edad única: la fruta y la verdura se introducen como parte de la alimentación complementaria, y en los menores de 6 meses se mantiene la lactancia materna o la fórmula [4]. A partir de esa edad, la SEUP recomienda una alimentación variada normal, con frutas y verduras entre los alimentos que se van añadiendo poco a poco [4]. En niños mayores, las frutas y verduras son bien toleradas y forman parte de la alimentación habitual [1]. Si tu hijo está estreñido, aumentar las comidas con fibra (frutas y verduras) ayuda a ablandar las deposiciones [4]. Consulta a tu pediatra si tienes dudas sobre cómo introducirlas o si el niño está decaído o vomita repetidamente [4][5].

text: El hundimiento de las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria y aparece descrito en las crisis asmáticas, según la SEUP: se les marcan las costillas y las clavículas al respirar (tiraje) y respiran más rápido de lo normal [4]. En una crisis asmática, administra de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol con cámara espaciadora, de una en una, y repite esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Mantén al niño en reposo, evita el humo del tabaco y la contaminación, y si toma tratamiento de mantenimiento, que lo siga tomando durante la crisis [6]. Si la crisis no cede tras el tratamiento en casa, o si te queda alguna duda, acude lo antes posible a un centro sanitario y lleva la cámara espaciadora [6].

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text: Sí, se puede: si el paracetamol no mejora el malestar a las 3-4 horas, es razonable dar ibuprofeno en su lugar, según la AEPap [6]. El ibuprofeno (Dalsy) es uno de los antitérmicos más usados y tiene una eficacia similar a la del paracetamol, según la SEUP [1]. No conviene alternarlos de forma sistemática cada 3-4 horas salvo que el niño tenga malestar antes de las 6 horas [1]. La dosis de ibuprofeno depende del peso, así que confirma la cantidad con tu pediatra o con el prospecto [6]. Consulta si está decaído, le cuesta respirar, tiene manchas que no desaparecen al presionar, no tolera líquidos o es menor de 2 meses [7].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text: Sí, puede seguir comiendo: no hace falta ayunar y los niños deben mantener una dieta prácticamente normal, salvo que un médico indique lo contrario, según la SEUP [7]. Conviene darle las comidas en cantidades más pequeñas y más frecuentes, respetando su apetito [7]. Es mejor evitar los alimentos muy grasos, los dulces y los zumos, y no hace falta quitar los lácteos [7]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación, ofreciéndole solución de rehidratación oral en tomas pequeñas y frecuentes [3]. q: mi hijo tiene manchas despues de tener fiebre, puede ser por la fiebre?
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día.

En un niño mayor, las manchas rojas en la piel después de la fiebre pueden ser un exantema, y lo importante es si desaparecen o no al presionarlas. Según la SEUP, hay que vigilar las petequias, que son puntos rojos que no desaparecen al apretar sus laterales [1], y las manchas que no se aclaran al presionarlas son motivo de consulta en urgencias [2]. También conviene vigilar que el niño esté activo, con buen color y sin dificultad para respirar [1][2].

Consulta sin esperar si las manchas no desaparecen al presionarlas, si el niño está decaído o muy irritable, o si le cuesta respirar [2].

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi bebe tiene muchos mocos y le cuesta dormir
text:
Los mocos y la tos son los síntomas típicos del catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica muy frecuente en los primeros años, según la SEUP [3]. La mucosidad puede durar hasta una semana, y la tos incluso más [4].

Para ayudar a dormir, se pueden hacer lavados nasales antes de las tomas y antes de dormir, preferiblemente con suero salino y nunca con agua del grifo [4]. Conviene ofrecerle líquidos abundantes y mantenerlo lejos del humo [4]. No le dé antitusivos, mucolíticos ni descongestivos, sobre todo si es menor de 6 años [4].

Consulte si le cuesta respirar, se le marcan las costillas o se le hunde el pecho, o si está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable [7].

q: mi hijo tiene tos pero no le cuesta respirar
text: La tos sin dificultad para respirar es lo habitual en un catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica de nariz y garganta muy frecuente en los primeros años, según la SEUP [6]. Es normal que los niños tengan entre 6 y 8 catarros al año, incluso más si van a la guardería [6]. En casa conviene vigilar el estado general y la aparición de dificultad para respirar, con respiraciones rápidas, costillas marcadas o pecho hundido, o dolor en el pecho al respirar [2]. Debe consultar si el niño empeora, está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable, o si aparece dificultad para respirar [2].

En un bebé, cualquier fiebre o una diarrea que dura más de un día también son motivo de consulta, según MedlinePlus [2].

q: que hago si mi hijo tiene una convulsion por fiebre
text:
Durante una convulsión febril, hay que tumbar al niño de lado en un sitio seguro, lejos de objetos con los que pueda golpearse, y no introducir nada en su boca, según la SEUP [3]. Conviene fijarse en los movimientos y en cuánto dura [3]. Cuando cede, se le coloca en posición lateral de seguridad y, si no ha recibido antitérmico en las últimas 2 horas, se le puede dar paracetamol o ibuprofeno [3]. Suele durar menos de 5 minutos y después el niño queda dormido o algo confuso un rato [3].

Consultar en urgencias si es la primera convulsión, si se repite, si se le ve muy dormido, confuso o irritable, o si hay dolor de cabeza intenso o vómitos repetidos [3].

q: mi hija vomito 4 veces y no quiere tomar suero
text:
Lo prioritario es asegurar que tome líquidos para evitar la deshidratación, según la SEUP [6]. Si vomita, espera 20 minutos y luego dale suero de rehidratación oral en pequeñas cantidades, 2-5 ml cada 5 minutos durante una hora [6]. Si lo tolera bien, puedes aumentar poco a poco la frecuencia [6]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos [6].

Consulta a tu pediatra si está decaída, vomita muchas veces o no toma líquidos [1]. Acude a urgencias si vomita mucho y no tolera nada, si los vómitos son verdosos o con sangre, o si está adormilada, tiene los ojos hundidos, llora sin lágrimas u orina poco [7].

text: Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día [1]. En un niño mayor, la fiebre suele durar entre 2 y 4 días y no es en sí misma señal de gravedad, según la SEUP [4]. Mientras tanto, lo importante es su comodidad: ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia, no lo fuerces a comer y no lo abrigues en exceso [5]. Puedes darle paracetamol o ibuprofeno a la dosis que te indique tu pediatra, sin alternarlos cada 3-4 horas [5]. No lo bañes en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos, porque resulta desagradable y no baja la fiebre [5]. Vigila su estado general y su color, y consulta si aparecen puntos rojos en la piel que no desaparecen al presionar [4].

text:
La nariz tapada es uno de los síntomas típicos del resfrío común, según MedlinePlus [1]. Esa congestión puede dificultar que el bebé tome el tetero, porque para succionar necesita respirar por la nariz.

Para evitar que se deshidrate, ofrécele líquidos con más frecuencia y en pequeñas cantidades; si le cuesta retenerlos, prueba con sorbos pequeños [2]. La leche materna o la fórmula siguen siendo su alimento principal [3].

Consulta a tu doctor si el bebé deja de mojar pañales, está muy somnoliento o irritable, o si la congestión dura más de 10 a 14 días [1].

q: como saber si mi hijo esta deshidratado
text: La deshidratación se reconoce por la pérdida de peso: hasta un 5 % es ligera, entre el 5 y el 10 % moderada, y entre el 10 y el 15 % grave, según Ecimed [3]. En casa puedes pesarlo sin ropa y comparar con su peso habitual; si no tienes báscula, no retrases la consulta por eso [3]. Los signos que se exploran son la pérdida de peso y el estado general en un examen minucioso [3]. En la deshidratación grave puede haber decaimiento marcado, y el tratamiento requiere ingreso hospitalario y rehidratación [1]. Consulta a tu doctor si sospechas deshidratación moderada o grave, o si el niño está muy decaído [1][3].

Que tu hijo haga menos de tres deposiciones a la semana, con heces duras y secas, es estreñimiento, según MedlinePlus [1]. En la mayoría de los casos dura poco y no es grave [1]. Ayuda ofrecerle más líquidos, sobre todo agua, y más comidas con fibra como frutas, verduras y cereales integrales, según la SEUP [3]. No sustituyas la fruta por zumos, porque tienen poca fibra [3]. Consulta a su pediatra si el estreñimiento no mejora con estos cambios, si tiene dolor de tripa importante, sangre en las heces, vómitos repetidos o si lo ves muy decaído [2][3].

q: mi hijo de 12 años se doblo el tobillo jugando al futbol y lo tiene morado
text:
Lo más probable es que sea un esguince: el tobillo se hincha o se amorata y duele al apoyarlo, según el NHS [1]. Durante los primeros 2 o 3 días sigue la terapia PRICE: protege la zona, reposo sin apoyar, hielo envuelto en un paño hasta 20 minutos cada 2 o 3 horas, vendaje de compresión y el pie elevado [6]. Mantén la zona amoratada elevada por encima del corazón y no sigas jugando ni usando la parte lesionada [4].

Acude a urgencias si oíste un crujido al lesionarse, el tobillo cambió de forma o está en ángulo raro, está dormido u hormiguea, o la piel se ve azulada, gris o fría al tacto: puede haber una fractura [7]. También si hay mucho dolor o hinchazón que empeora, o no puede apoyar el peso ni caminar más de unos pasos [3].

No mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más es una señal de deshidratación en bebés y niños pequeños, según MedlinePlus [3]. La deshidratación puede ser leve o lo suficientemente grave como para poner en peligro la vida [3].

Si el bebé deja de mojar pañales, conviene que lo vea un profesional de la salud lo antes posible [4].

q: mi hijo tiene manchas rojas despues de la fiebre
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

Después de la fiebre es frecuente que aparezcan manchas rojas en la piel, y lo importante es comprobar si desaparecen al presionar. Según la SEUP, hay que vigilar la aparición de petequias, que son puntos rojos que no desaparecen al apretar en sus laterales [1]. La prueba del vaso consiste en poner un vaso transparente encima de la mancha y apretar: si no desaparece, son petequias [6].

Consulta sin demora si las manchas no se aclaran al presionarlas, si el niño está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, o si le cuesta respirar [2].

q: y la puc cuanto recomienda para la tos
text:
No hay una dosis de jarabe para la tos que se recomiende: no use anticatarrales ni jarabes para la tos, sobre todo si el niño es menor de 6 años, según la SEUP [6]. Tampoco se deben administrar jarabes ni supositorios para la tos sin consultar con su pediatra [5].

Lo que sí ayuda en casa es ofrecer abundantes líquidos y hacer lavados nasales con suero salino, nunca con agua del grifo [6]. La tos puede durar más de una semana y forma parte de la evolución normal del catarro [6].

Consulte si aparece dificultad para respirar, el niño está decaído o muy irritable, o si tiene dificultad para tragar o babea mucho [3][5].

text:

Ein Arzt kann bei stärkeren Beschwerden ein Mittel gegen Übelkeit oder Erbrechen verordnen [2].

Wenden Sie sich bei diesen Warnzeichen sofort an Ihren Arzt, laut MedlinePlus [3]:

text:

Schwere Fälle werden im Krankenhaus mit Flüssigkeit über die Vene behandelt [1].

Warnzeichen, bei denen Sie ärztlichen Rat suchen sollten: dunkler, übel riechender Urin oder selteneres Wasserlassen als sonst, laut NHS [3]. Wenn Sie den Eindruck haben, dass Ihr Kind stark ausgetrocknet ist, rufen Sie Ihren Arzt an [4].

q: mein Baby hat rote Flecken am Bauch und kratzt sich

Rote Flecken am Bauch, die jucken, können bei einem atypischen Verlauf der Hand-Fuß-Mund-Krankheit auftreten, so das RKI [6]. Normalerweise zeigt sich der Ausschlag dort nicht juckend an Handflächen und Fußsohlen, bei atypischen Verläufen aber auch am Gesäß und als stark juckender Ausschlag [6]. Die Krankheit verläuft meist mild, und fast alle Erkrankten erholen sich innerhalb von 5 bis 7 Tagen ohne ärztliche Behandlung [6].

Bei einem juckenden Ausschlag am ganzen Körper oder wenn das Baby trinkt schlecht, sollten Sie Ihr Kind ärztlich untersuchen lassen.

q: mein Kind hat Fieber nach der Impfung
text:
Wenn Ihr Kind jünger als 3 Monate ist, muss Fieber noch am selben Tag ärztlich abgeklärt werden [2].

Bei älteren Kindern ist Fieber nach einer Impfung möglich: Zu den Ursachen erhöhter Temperatur gehören neben Infekten auch Impfungen, so die NHS [2]. Fieber ist meist Ausdruck der körpereigenen Abwehr und kein Zeichen einer Krankheit für sich [3]. Die Temperatur wird in der Regel innerhalb von 1 bis 4 Tagen wieder normal [1]. Geben Sie kein Aspirin an Kinder unter 16 Jahren [2]. Die Dosis von Fiebermitteln richtet sich nach Alter und Gewicht; fragen Sie dazu Ihre Ärztin oder Ihren Arzt.

Suchen Sie ärztliche Hilfe, wenn das Fieber länger als 5 Tage anhält, Ihr Kind nicht trinken will, weniger nasse Windeln hat oder Ihnen nicht wie sonst erscheint [2].

q: pourquoi ai je de la fièvre alors que c est mon fils qui est malade
text:
Si votre enfant a moins de 3 mois et de la fièvre, il doit voir un médecin le jour même [2].

Pour un enfant plus grand, la fièvre est une réaction naturelle du corps qui lutte contre une infection, et elle redescend généralement en 1 à 4 jours [1][4]. Le fait que vous ayez vous aussi de la fièvre ne s'explique pas par la maladie de votre fils : les infections qui donnent de la fièvre se transmettent d'une personne à l'autre, et rien ne dit que vous partagez la même [4]. La grippe, par exemple, se manifeste par de la fièvre, une toux et des douleurs musculaires [6].

Consultez un médecin si la fièvre dure 5 jours ou plus, si votre enfant ne veut pas manger ou n'est pas comme d'habitude, ou s'il est déshydraté [2].

Quel âge a votre enfant ? Avec l'âge, je peux préciser la réponse.

Un nez bouché et une baisse de l'alimentation font partie des symptômes habituels d'une infection respiratoire chez le nourrisson, selon le NHS [4]. La plupart du temps il s'agit de symptômes de rhume, qui s'améliorent en quelques jours [4].

En attendant, la SEUP conseille des lavages de nez pour garder le nez libre, des tétées fractionnées — petites et fréquentes — pour maintenir une bonne alimentation et hydratation, et la position semi-inclinée pour faciliter la respiration [3]. Il faut aussi éviter strictement l'exposition à la fumée de tabac [3].

Consultez votre médecin si votre bébé s'alimente beaucoup moins que d'habitude, s'il est très fatigué ou irritable, ou si sa respiration devient difficile [4].

q: mon fils est tombé du lit mais joue normalement
text: Votre fils a fait un choc à la tête, et la plupart des traumatismes crâniens sont légers et ne représentent pas de danger, selon la SEUP [4]. Il faut surveiller l'apparition de symptômes dans les premières 24 heures : maux de tête intenses ou qui ne cèdent pas au paracétamol ou à l'ibuprofène, vomissements répétés, confusion ou désorientation, irritabilité ou difficulté à le réveiller, changements de comportement, difficulté à parler ou à marcher, ou encore du sang ou un liquide clair qui sort du nez ou des oreilles [3]. Consultez aux urgences s'il présente l'un de ces symptômes, si son comportement vous inquiète, s'il a moins de trois mois, ou si la chute a été de plus d'un mètre [2]. On recommande 24 à 48 heures de repos physique et mental, sans sport ni écrans, puis une reprise progressive [3]. Il peut dormir, mais pour un choc important il est conseillé de le réveiller toutes les 4 heures [5].

Para uma criança maior, febre após a vacina costuma ser uma reação esperada: as vacinas estimulam o sistema de defesa do organismo e podem causar reações, segundo o Ministério da Saúde [3]. As vacinas oferecidas pelo SUS são seguras e eficazes, e seguem sendo monitoradas quanto à qualidade, segurança e eficácia [3]. q: meu bebe caiu do sofa e bateu a cabeça (idade: 1 ano) (peso: 11 kg)
text:
Depois de uma queda com golpe na cabeça, os sintomas mais comuns são dor de cabeça, confusão, sensação de tontura, náuseas, vômitos e sonolência, segundo a SEUP [1]. É importante vigiar o bebê nas primeiras 24 horas para detectar sinais de gravidade [3]. A maioria dos traumatismos cranianos é leve e não representa perigo [3].

Vá ao pronto-socorro se houver:

- Vômitos repetidos, desorientação ou confusão, ou, em bebês muito pequenos, irritabilidade ou dificuldade para acordar [2].
- Sangramento ou saída de líquido claro pelo nariz ou pelos ouvidos [2].
- Convulsões, perda de consciência, fala arrastada, fraqueza ou falta de coordenação, ou uma pupila maior que a outra [4].
- Choro que não para e não consola, ou recusa de mamar ou comer [4].

Se tiver dor de cabeça, pode-se dar ibuprofeno ou paracetamol nas doses indicadas pelo médico [6]. Pode dormir, mas em traumatismos mais importantes é recomendável acordá-lo a cada 4 horas [6].

Não é preciso acordar a criança para dar o remédio se ela estiver dormindo [3]. Procure atendimento se a febre não melhorar com o antitérmico ou se surgirem sinais de alarme [3].

q: minha filha está com diarreia há dois dias
text:
A diarreia geralmente melhora sozinha, com repouso e bastante líquido e eletrólitos, segundo a MedlinePlus [2]. O mais importante é evitar a desidratação, oferecendo soluções de rehidratação oral já preparadas, e não soluções caseiras nem refrigerantes [4]. A criança pode continuar comendo uma dieta praticamente normal, em porções menores e mais frequentes, evitando alimentos gordurosos, doces e sucos [5]. Não dê remédios para diarreia ou vômito sem consultar o pediatra [4].

Procure atendimento se a diarreia durar mais de um dia em bebês ou mais de dois dias em crianças maiores, se houver febre, vômitos frequentes, sangue nas fezes, ou sinais de desidratação como boca seca, urinar pouco ou não molhar as fraldas por 3 horas ou mais [1].

q: o meu filho tem tosse seca sobretudo à noite
text:
A tosse seca que piora à noite ou de madrugada é um dos sintomas da asma em crianças, segundo o MedlinePlus [6]. A otite média aguda é a infeção e inflamação do ouvido médio, situado atrás do tímpano, e costuma surgir como complicação de uma constipação com muita mucosidade nasal, segundo a SEUP [5]. É uma das infeções mais frequentes em crianças com menos de 2 anos [5].

Alguns sinais de que deve falar com o seu médico: febre que dura mais de 4 dias, sintomas que duram mais de 10 dias sem melhorar, ou sintomas que melhoram e depois voltam a piorar [6]. Também deve procurar ajuda se a criança tiver dificuldade em respirar ou respirar muito depressa [6].

q: o meu filho teve febre depois das vacinas
text:
Se a criança tiver menos de 3 meses, febre precisa de avaliação médica no mesmo dia. Num bebé mais velho, a febre depois das vacinas é uma reação possível e costuma passar sozinha.

As vacinas são seguras e eficazes, e a febre pode surgir como resposta normal do organismo, segundo o Ministério da Saúde [1]. Mantenha a criança confortável, com pouca roupa e boa ingestão de líquidos.

Não dê nenhum medicamento sem falar com o médico: a dose depende da idade e do peso da criança. Se a febre durar mais de 48 a 72 horas, vier muito alta ou a criança estiver muito irritada, sem apetite ou com outros sintomas, procure um serviço de saúde.

Que idade tem? Com a idade afino a resposta.

Se houver pouca ou nenhuma urina, confusão, desmaio, batimentos ou respiração rápidos, procure ajuda médica imediatamente [1].

Para repor os líquidos, existem soluções de rehidratação oral para crianças que se compram sem receita [5]. Não use soluções caseiras nem refrigerantes para repor as perdas, e não dê remédios para diarreia ou vômito sem falar com o pediatra, segundo a SEUP [6].

q: posso dar brufen ao mesmo tempo
text:
Não, os antitérmicos não devem ser alternados de forma sistemática, segundo a AEPap [4][5]. Só se, 3 a 4 horas depois de dar um antitérmico, a temperatura continuar alta e o mal-estar não melhorar, é razoável trocá-lo — por exemplo, começar com paracetamol e, na toma seguinte, dar ibuprofeno em vez de paracetamol [2][4].

O ibuprofeno pode ser dado a cada 6 a 8 horas e não deve ser usado se houver vómitos contínuos, nem em crianças com menos de 3 meses ou menos de 5 kg [4]. A dose calcula-se pelo peso, não pela idade [4]. Siga as indicações do seu pediatra e do folheto do medicamento [2].

q: a minha filha de 2 anos tem uma tosse de cão durante a noite
text: A tosse de cão à noite pode ser um sinal de coqueluche, uma infecção respiratória causada por bactéria cuja principal característica são crises de tosse seca, segundo o Ministério da Saúde [4]. Na coqueluche, a tosse fica muito forte e incontrolável, com crises súbitas que podem causar vômitos e dificuldade para inspirar, e essa fase pode durar de duas a seis semanas [1]. O diagnóstico no início é difícil, porque os sintomas podem parecer um resfriado, e a tosse seca é um forte indicativo [3]. Procure o serviço de saúde para avaliação: crianças pequenas podem ter formas mais graves, e o médico pode pedir exames para confirmar [1][3].

q: quando começar a dar alimentos sólidos ao bebé
text: Por volta dos 6 meses de idade, as necessidades de energia e nutrientes do bebê começam a superar o que o leite materno oferece, e é preciso introduzir outros alimentos, segundo a OMS [2]. Comece com pequenas quantidades aos 6 meses e aumente aos poucos, conforme o bebê cresce [2]. No início, o mais importante não é a quantidade que ele come, mas se acostumar com a ideia de comer; ele ainda recebe a maior parte da energia e dos nutrientes do leite materno ou da fórmula [3]. Ofereça variedade de alimentos junto com o leite, e vá aumentando a quantidade e a variedade até que ele coma os mesmos alimentos da família, em porções menores [3]. Se o bebê nasceu prematuro, peça orientação ao seu médico sobre quando começar [3].

q: o bebé tem o nariz entupido e custa-lhe mamar
text:
O nariz entupido é comum em quadros respiratórios leves, como o resfriado, e costuma durar de 10 a 14 dias, segundo a MedlinePlus [2]. Para ajudar o bebê a mamar e respirar melhor, a SEUP recomenda lavagens nasais para manter o nariz livre de muco, mamadas pequenas e frequentes para manter boa alimentação e hidratação, e deixá-lo em posição semiincorporada [3]. Evite rigorosamente a exposição à fumaça de tabaco e reforce a lavagem das mãos entre os familiares [3].

Procure atendimento se houver dificuldade para respirar, se ele mamar ou beber muito menos que o habitual, ou se estiver muito irritado ou com menos atividade [5][6].

q: o meu bebé caiu do muda fraldas e fez um galo na cabeça
text:
O galo na cabeça é um traumatismo craniano, o termo médico para um golpe na cabeça causado geralmente por uma queda, segundo a SEUP [1]. Os sintomas mais comuns são dor de cabeça, confusão, sensação de tontura, náuseas, vômitos e sonolência [1]. É importante vigiar o bebê nas primeiras 24 horas após o golpe [3].

Procure o serviço de urgências se houver dor de cabeça intensa ou que não melhora, vômitos repetidos, desorientação ou confusão, irritabilidade ou dificuldade para acordar, mudanças de comportamento, dificuldade para falar ou andar, ou saída de sangue ou líquido claro pelo nariz ou pelos ouvidos [2]. Também se recomenda ir se o bebê tiver menos de três meses ou se a queda foi de uma altura superior a um metro [7].

q: quando posso começar a dar sólidos ao bebé
text:
Por volta dos 6 meses de idade, segundo a OMS [2]. Nessa fase, as necessidades de energia e nutrientes do bebé começam a superar o que o leite materno oferece, e por isso são necessários alimentos complementares [2].

O NHS indica começar por volta dos 6 meses, começando com pequenas quantidades e aumentando aos poucos a quantidade e a variedade [3]. No início, importa mais o bebé habituar-se à ideia de comer do que a quantidade que come — ele continua a receber a maior parte da energia do leite materno ou da fórmula [3].

A AEP lembra que nenhum método respeitoso com o bebé é melhor que outro, seja puré ou alimentação guiada pelo próprio bebé [6]. Se o bebé nasceu prematuro, convém pedir orientação ao seu médico sobre quando começar [3].

q: طفلي يسعل كثيرا في الليل
text:
السعال المستمر، وخاصة أثناء الليل، من الأعراض الشائعة للربو، وفقاً لمنظمة الصحة العالمية [1]. وقد تكون أعراض الربو أسوأ ليلاً أو أثناء التمارين الرياضية [1]. ومن الأعراض الأخرى الأزيز عند الزفير، وضيق أو صعوبة في التنفس، وضيق في الصدر [1]. ويجب على من تظهر عليه هذه الأعراض التحدث إلى مقدم الرعاية الصحية [1].

يجب مراجعة الطبيب إذا كان الطفل شديد التهيّج أو النعاس، أو شاحباً أو مزرقّاً، أو إذا ازدادت صعوبة التنفس، أو احتاج إلى جلسات استنشاق متكررة كل ساعتين أو أقل، وفقاً لـ SEUP [7].

q: mon enfant de 3 ans a la diarrhée depuis 3 jours et est très fatigué
text:
La diarrhée se définit par au moins trois selles molles ou liquides par jour, et elle est en général le symptôme d'une infection intestinale, selon l'OMS [1]. Elle se traite avec des sels de réhydratation orale, une solution d'eau propre, de sucre et de sel [1]. Un complément de zinc pendant 10 à 14 jours raccourcit l'épisode et en améliore l'issue [1].

La fatigue peut accompagner une diarrhée, mais chez un enfant de 3 ans qui a la diarrhée depuis 3 jours et qui est très fatigué, il faut le faire voir par votre médecin, surtout s'il boit peu, urine peu ou semble s'affaiblir.
sources: [1] WHO — "Maladies diarréhiques", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/fr/news-room/fact-sheets/det

q: mon fils de 4 ans a des boutons rouges qui démangent partout
text:
Les démangeaisons et les boutons rouges qui grattent partout peuvent correspondre à la gale, selon l'OMS : elle provoque de fortes démangeaisons, souvent plus intenses la nuit, et une éruption cutanée [5]. Chez les jeunes enfants, l'éruption peut être plus étendue, notamment sur la paume des mains, la plante des pieds et le cuir chevelu [5]. La gale se traite par une crème ou des médicaments par voie orale [6].

Consultez votre médecin pour confirmer et traiter, car le grattage peut entraîner une infection de la peau [5].

q: mon bébé de 10 mois tousse beaucoup et a la poitrine qui siffle
text:
Chez un bébé de 10 mois, une toux avec un sifflement de la poitrine correspond à ce que la SEUP décrit comme des sifflements (« sibilancias »), causés par une obstruction des bronches [3]. Chez les jeunes enfants, la cause principale de ces sifflements est une infection respiratoire virale, comme un rhume [3]. Ces épisodes ne signifient pas que votre bébé sera asthmatique plus tard [3].

Consultez votre médecin, car les symptômes d'asthme chez le nourrisson peuvent aussi inclure une difficulté à manger ou à téter [4].

q: quand donner de la bouillie à un bébé de 5 mois
text: Non, à 5 mois on ne donne pas encore de bouillie : la recommandation est de garder le lait maternel comme alimentation exclusive pendant les six premiers mois [4], et d'introduire les aliments progressivement autour du sixième mois, jamais avant le quatrième [6]. La diversification se fait alors un aliment à la fois, selon les habitudes de la famille [6]. Si votre bébé est né prématurément, le moment doit être individualisé avec le médecin, car les repères des bébés nés à terme ne s'appliquent pas directement [1]. Parlez-en à votre médecin avant de commencer.

q: ابنتي لديها ألم في الأذن بعد الزكام
text: ألم الأذن بعد الزكام شائع جداً عند الأطفال، وغالباً ما يتحسّن من تلقاء نفسه خلال 3 أيام، وفقاً لـ NHS [5]. التهاب الأذن الوسطى تحديداً يسبّبه فيروسات مثل الزكام والإنفلونزا [5]. تشمل الأعراض عادةً ألماً داخل الأذن وارتفاعاً في الحرارة وصعوبة في السمع، وقد يشدّ الطفل أذنه أو يكون سريع الانفعال أو قليل الأكل [5]. معظم التهابات الأذن تزول خلال 3 أيام، وقد تستمر الأعراض أحياناً حتى أسبوع [5]. راجعي الطبيب إذا استمر الألم أو ارتفعت الحرارة أو لم تتحسّن ابنتك [5].

q: mon fils dort tout le temps et n arrive pas à ouvrir les yeux
banner: 🚨 Appelez tout de suite le numéro d'urgence de votre pays (112 dans l'UE, 911 en Amérique) ou allez aux urgences. | Raison: Ne répond pas aux stimulations
text:
Un enfant qui reste dans un seul état de conscience pendant la journée, sans alterner éveil et sommeil, est anormal et doit être examiné, selon le PUC Chile [6]. Ne pas ouvrir les yeux fait partie des signes que cette équipe décrit dans l'évaluation du comportement [2]. Le PUC Chile indique aussi qu'un enfant qui ne répond pas ou reste apathique peut refléter un état neurologique anormal [2].

En attendant les secours, gardez-le sur le côté et ne mettez rien dans sa bouche.

Une forte fièvre est très fréquente chez le jeune enfant et revient généralement à la normale en 1 à 4 jours, selon le NHS [3]. Un norovirus provoque des vomissements qui s'améliorent habituellement en deux jours environ [5]. Continuez à lui proposer à boire souvent, par petites quantités.

Consultez sans attendre si votre enfant ne peut plus rien boire ni garder, s'il est très somnolent ou difficile à réveiller, ou s'il a des convulsions [7].

q: сын кашляет уже неделю, особенно ночью
text: Кашель, который усиливается ночью, бывает при астме у детей — это один из её симптомов, по данным MedlinePlus [2]. При астматическом приступе кашель может быть сильным, появляется тяжёлое дыхание, а бледность или синеватый цвет лица, губ и ногтей — признак того, что нужно немедленно обратиться за медицинской помощью [2]. При ларингите дети тоже часто кашляют по ночам и плохо спят, и обычно всё проходит за несколько дней, но может длиться до недели, по данным SEUP [4]. Следите за дыханием ребёнка и его общим состоянием: если дышать становится трудно, это повод показать его врачу [4]. Если кашель держится больше 10 дней без улучшения, поговорите с врачом [6].
sources: [2] MedlinePlus — "Asma en niños", section "¿Cuáles son los síntomas del asma en los niños

q: у ребенка красные пятна на ногах и они сильно чешутся
text:
Красные пятна на ногах, которые сильно чешутся, могут быть крапивницей — аллергической реакцией; по данным NHS, крапивницу обычно можно лечить дома [1]. Если вокруг рта появляется отёк или ребёнку трудно дышать, нужна срочная помощь [1].

Обратитесь к врачу, если сыпь не проходит, распространяется или ребёнку становится хуже.
sources: [1] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Raised, itchy spots or patches"

q: у ребенка запор после начала прикорма
text: Запор — это когда стул реже трёх раз в неделю, кал может быть твёрдым и сухим, а иногда болезненным, по данным MedlinePlus [1]. У большинства детей он длится недолго и не опасен [1]. При запоре после начала прикорма главное — больше жидкости, лучше воды, и больше продуктов с клетчаткой: фруктов, овощей, круп и хлеба с отрубями, по данным SEUP [2]. Фрукты не заменяйте соками — в них мало клетчатки [2]. Не давайте слабительные или клизмы без совета педиатра [2]. Обратитесь к врачу, если появилась сильная боль в животе, кровь в стуле, ребёнок вялый или его многократно рвёт [2].

q: у ребенка поднялась температура после прививки
text:
Если ребёнку меньше 3 месяцев, температура требует осмотра врачом в тот же день.

У детей постарше температура после прививки — известная реакция: вакцина MenB может вызывать жар, и по данным nidirect дома стоит иметь детский парацетамол ещё до прививки [6]. Дозу парацетамола должен подсказать врач — она зависит от веса ребёнка [6]. Возраст, в котором делают прививки, в России определяется национальным календарём профилактических прививок.

Обратиться к врачу нужно, если у ребёнка очень высокая температура, рвота или понос в день прививки, либо если была плохая реакция на предыдущую прививку [4]. При сыпи, зуде, затруднённом дыхании или обмороке после прививки помощь нужна немедленно [6].

Сколько лет ребёнку? Зная возраст, я отвечу точнее.
